attempts.summary: Built the lan-a/lan-b topology on node1 (OPNsense) using its two spare interfaces (vtnet1=opt1/lan-a 10.50.10.1/24, vtnet2=opt2/lan-b 10.50.20.1/24), addressed node2's enp8s0 (10.50.10.11/24, lan-a) and node3's enp8s0 (10.50.20.12/24, lan-b) via NetworkManager persistent profiles, added cross-subnet static routes on node2/node3 via node1, and added firewall pass rules for opt1/opt2 plus a hybrid-mode outbound NAT rule (source 10.50.10.0/24, interface opt2, target=interface address) so node2->node3 traffic is source-NATed to node1's opt2 address 10.50.20.1 while node3->node2 traffic keeps its original source. Verified via tcpdump on node3's and node2's LAN interfaces during live TCP sessions. Then executed the mandatory node-restart protocol on all three nodes one at a time (node2, node3, node1), confirming boot-identity changes (Linux boot_id / FreeBSD kern.boottime) and re-verifying interface config, firewall/NAT rules, routing, and the asymmetric-NAT behavior end-to-end after all restarts.
